title: Research: Python AST and syntax for refactoring test coverage
description: Gather and summarize information about Python's AST structure, tricky syntax edge cases, commenting and whitespace rules, name resolution rules, and module dependency patterns relevant to jedi's refactoring operations. Output: a checked-in document at docs/refactor_research.md that other agents can use to find gaps in test coverage.
close_reason: Research complete. Document at docs/refactor_research.md covers: AST assignment variants, operator precedence/parenthesization, comments/whitespace, LEGB edge cases, module/import patterns, async/await, f-strings, type annotations, decorators, special statement forms, and per-refactor gap analysis for all six refactors.

description: Add introduce_field to jedi's refactoring toolkit. Takes a local variable/expression inside a method and promotes it to an instance field (self.x), updating callers.

title: Implement Introduce Parameter refactoring (Core 6)

title: review 99f81bf3: introduce.py duplicates helpers from refactoring/__init__.py
description:
Commit 99f81bf3 (Add introduce_parameter and introduce_field) added jedi/api/refactoring/introduce.py with two issues:

1. _remove_indent_of_prefix() at line 275 of introduce.py is a verbatim copy of _remove_indent_of_prefix() in jedi/api/refactoring/__init__.py (line 277). The function should be imported from __init__.py instead.

2. _rename_references() and _replace_references_with_field() are structurally identical tree-walking functions that differ only in the action taken on a matched name node. The shared skeleton (try/except AttributeError, guard for funcdef/classdef/trailer-dot) should be factored into a single walk helper that accepts a callback, or the two functions should be unified.

Neither issue affects correctness, but both create maintenance burden: a bug fix in the shared logic must be applied in two (or three) places.

title: review 48c37298: _is_safe_without_parens uses type-name heuristics, not precedence
description:
Commit 48c37298 (fix inline adding unnecessary parens) introduced _is_safe_without_parens() which checks a hardcoded list of node type names:

    if rhs.type in ('number', 'string', 'keyword', 'fstring'):
        return True
    if rhs.type == 'name':
        return True
    if rhs.type == 'atom' and hasattr(rhs, 'children') and rhs.children:
        first_child = rhs.children[0]
        if hasattr(first_child, 'value') and first_child.value in ('(', '[', '{'):
            return True
    return False

This approach has two problems:

1. It is a heuristic: it enumerates safe cases rather than reasoning from the AST structure. Whether parens are needed depends on the *context* (what expression the inlined value appears in) and the *precedence* of the inlined expression, not just whether the expression is a simple atom. The existing 'needs_parens' logic already captures the context; what's missing is a proper precedence comparison.

2. It uses hasattr() for duck-typing rather than parso's BaseNode/Leaf distinction or isinstance checks. Parso nodes always have .children (non-leaf) or .value (leaf) — defensive hasattr checks obscure this.

The fix should either: (a) extend the type-name list more carefully with tests for each added type, or (b) replace the heuristic with a precedence table keyed on node types (the principled approach). At minimum, add tests for cases not yet covered: unary expressions (x = -1), attribute access (x = a.b), subscript (x = a[0]).

title: review 3b431cf3+6030d2c9: _FRIENDLY_TYPE_NAMES fstring_start is dead code
description:
Commits 3b431cf3 (error message improvements) and 6030d2c9 (f-string extraction fix) were applied in sequence, leaving dead code.

3b431cf3 added _FRIENDLY_TYPE_NAMES = {'fstring_start': 'f-string', ...} to produce a better error message when the user tries to extract an fstring_start node.

6030d2c9 then added fstring_start to _is_not_extractable_syntax(), which causes cursor-climbing to the parent fstring node before _is_expression_with_error() is ever called. So the error path that would use _FRIENDLY_TYPE_NAMES['fstring_start'] is now unreachable — the node will have been promoted to 'fstring' (which IS in _VARIABLE_EXCTRACTABLE) before the check runs.

Additionally: there is no longer an error test for attempting to extract a sub-expression inside an f-string (e.g., extracting 'a' from 'f"val={a}"'). The old fstring-error test was removed by 6030d2c9 and not replaced. Add a test for this case and clarify what the expected behavior is (error or a different kind of climbing).

title: review d531a55b: _contains_await has dead await_expr branch
description:
Commit d531a55b (Fix extract_function for async) introduced _contains_await() in jedi/api/refactoring/extract.py. The function has a dead branch:

    else:
        if node.type == 'await_expr':   # dead code
            return True

Parso does NOT use an 'await_expr' node type. 'await x()' is parsed as atom_expr([<Keyword: await>, <Name: x>, <trailer: ()>]). The 'await' keyword is a leaf node, so it is found via the 'except AttributeError' branch. The 'await_expr' check in the else branch is unreachable.

The function works correctly despite the dead code, but the dead branch creates confusion about parso's AST structure. Fix: remove the dead 'await_expr' branch and add a comment explaining that parso represents 'await expr' as an atom_expr whose first child is a keyword leaf with value 'await'.

Also: no test for extracting code that contains a bare 'await' keyword without a call (e.g. 'await fut'), or for async generators.

title: introduce_field: add test confirming first-param name used for self
description:
Comment on commit 99f81bf: 'How do we determine whether it has a self parameter? Hopefully we are not just looking for a parameter named "self"?'

The code uses params[0].name.value — the name of the first parameter, whatever it is. The existing cls-param test already covers 'cls'. The code is correct.

Action: add a test using a non-conventional first parameter name (e.g. 'this') to further document that any first-parameter name is supported, not just 'self' or 'cls'.

title: introduce_parameter: document call-site behavior
description:
Comment on commit 99f81bf: 'I've noticed all of these tests are only checking the local function. What happens at the call site? Is it always possible to omit the new parameter?'

Since introduce_parameter always adds a default value (the original RHS), all existing call sites remain valid without modification — callers can omit the new parameter and the default will be used. This is correct and intentional design behavior.

Action: add a test case that includes a call site, verifying it is unchanged after the refactoring, to document that this is expected.

title: introduce_field/parameter: fix _find_enclosing_funcdef crossing class boundaries
description:
Comment on commit 99f81bf: 'Aren't there other types of constructs that could interfere with the binding of the name to the function? For example:
    def a():
        class Foo:
            b=7
b is a class attribute of Foo, not a local variable in a().'

Bug: _find_enclosing_funcdef traverses upward through classdef nodes. If a variable is defined inside a nested class (e.g. Foo.b), the function incorrectly returns the outer method (a), causing introduce_parameter to add 'b' as a parameter of 'a' and remove it from Foo's body.

Fix: make _find_enclosing_funcdef return None when it encounters a classdef before finding a funcdef. Add nested-class-var-error tests to both introduce_field.py and introduce_parameter.py.

title: introduce_parameter: reject call expressions as default values
description:
Comment on commit 99f81bf: 'This is also a bug. In the original function, bar() would be called on every invocation. In the new function, bar() gets called during function definition and then never again.'

introduce_parameter currently accepts call expressions (e.g. x = bar()) as defaults, producing semantically different code. bar() would be evaluated once at function definition time instead of each call.

Fix: raise RefactoringError when the RHS is a call expression (atom_expr with a call trailer). Change test case call-default from 'text' to 'error' expectation.

title: introduce_parameter: reject mutable default values
description:
Comments on commit 99f81bf:
- 'This is a bug. A parameter default that is not a primitive will retain its identity from one function call to the next. If foo() appended to the item list, for example, then the next call to foo() would see that larger list.'
- 'Obviously only an issue if the default is mutable.'

introduce_parameter currently accepts mutable literals (lists, dicts, sets) as defaults, producing semantically different code. A parameter default of [1,2,3] shares the same list across all calls, whereas the original local variable created a fresh list each time.

Fix: raise RefactoringError for mutable literal defaults (atom nodes with '[' or '{' as first child). Change test cases list-default and dict-default from 'text' to 'error' expectations.

title: introduce_field: remove redundant type-value tests
description:
Comment on commit 99f81bf: 'Are these <type>-value tests interesting? Aren't they just all opaque expressions, as far as the refactoring code is concerned?'

The tests string-value, expression-value, list-value, none-value, dict-value, bool-value in test/refactor/introduce_field.py don't test anything different from 'simple'. The refactoring code treats the RHS as an opaque string regardless of type. Remove these redundant tests.

title: introduce_field: error when field already exists
description:
Comment on commit 99f81bf: 'What if there is already a field named x?'

If self.x already exists in the method, introduce_field should raise an error rather than introducing a conflicting second assignment.

Implement: check for existing self.{var_name} references in the function body before proceeding. Add test 'field-already-exists-error' to test/refactor/introduce_field.py.

title: extract_function from async body produces non-async function
description: When extracting an expression containing await from an async function, the extracted function is created as a regular def (not async def) and the call site omits await. The extracted code will fail at runtime since await is used outside async context. Rope handles this by making the extracted function async.
close_reason: Fixed: extract_function now produces async def and await calls when extracting code with await expressions

title: rename with nonlocal doesn't update nonlocal declaration or outer scope
description: When renaming a variable that has a nonlocal declaration, jedi renames the assignment and local uses but does NOT update: (1) the nonlocal x declaration itself, (2) references in the outer scope (e.g., return x). This produces broken code. Discovered during probe testing. Rope handles this correctly.

title: Inline adds double parens around already-parenthesized expressions
description: When inlining a = (1 + 2) used as 'test(a * 3)', produces 'test(((1 + 2)) * 3)' instead of 'test((1 + 2) * 3)'. The outer parens of the rhs are included in replace_code and then another layer is added by the parens logic.
close_reason: Fixed: already-parenthesized expressions no longer double-wrapped during inline

title: Inline adds unnecessary parens around simple literals
description: When inlining x = 42 in 'return x + 1', produces 'return (42) + 1' instead of 'return 42 + 1'. The parens are added because tree_name.parent.type is in EXPRESSION_PARTS (arith_expr), but a simple literal doesn't need wrapping.
close_reason: Fixed: simple literals no longer wrapped in parens during inline
